title: Pricing isn’t one number.
description:
Most sellers think pricing is one number. It's actually four, and picking the wrong one quietly costs you.
Here's the real math nobody explains. For any home there's a range, not a single "correct" price. Price at the top and you might squeeze more, but you'll likely sit longer and risk chasing the market down. Price toward the bottom and you'll move with more competition, but you may leave money on the table. In between sit the tiers where most of the strategy actually lives.
None of those is automatically right. The right tier depends on your timeline, your equity, and how much certainty you want. That's a decision only you can make, and only if someone shows you all four honestly instead of selling you the highest one just to win your listing.
That's what I lay out. Four tiers, the tradeoff on each, and what each one likely means for your days on market and your bottom line. Then you choose with your eyes open.
